claims.text: The initial nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts are disordered FCC solid solutions.
The initial catalyst has an approximately equiatomic distribution of Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os.
Increasing the Rh fraction while decreasing another component such as Ir modifies local lattice distortions.
Increasing the Rh fraction enhances or otherwise modifies orbital hybridization in the catalyst.
The altered Rh content and orbital hybridization shift the active-site d-band center closer to the Fermi level.
The d-band-center shift changes the adsorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates such as CO and CH3CO species.
Optimized intermediate adsorption facilitates more complete ethanol oxidation to CO2.
Optimized intermediate adsorption reduces deleterious carbonaceous surface poisoning.
A higher-Rh catalyst will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation current density than the equiatomic baseline.
A higher-Rh catalyst will produce more CO2 and fewer partially oxidized products than the equiatomic baseline.
A higher-Rh catalyst will lose less activity during potential cycling than the equiatomic baseline.
The proposed mechanism is expected to hold in acidic electrolyte at room temperature and moderate ethanol concentration.
Changes in pH, extreme temperatures, or substantially altered reaction environments may change adsorption energetics and catalytic behavior.
